newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Weather good in key Brazil soybean states - coops.
newsitem.headline: Weather good in key Brazil soybean states - coops.

text.p: Conditions appeared to be normalising in Brazil's key soybean growing regions with temperatures dropping and growers hopeful that the threat of drought had been averted for now.

"Now the situation will normalise itself," said Ivo Didone of the Rio Grande do Sul agricultural secretariat. "The rains last weekend reached practically the entire state and partly resolved the problem of drought."
But a long dry spell between December 20 and January 18 had stunted some plants and caused them to flower early.
"Without a doubt there will be a 10 percent drop in the total harvest of this state," Didone said.
In Candelaria, one of the areas worst affected by the hot weather, rains had restored some humidity and growers were cautiously confident.
"The situation has improved," said Marcos Ricardo Streck, agronomist at the Cotrican cooperative. "The soybeans are starting to flower."
Streck said the next rainfall was forecast for January 24 and currently the maximum temperature was 30 degrees Celsius.

"Things are much better and it's still raining," said Leonidas Cesar Dutra, agronomist at the Coppal cooperative in Paim Filho. "Conditions are quite humid and temperatures have dropped to 22 or 23 degrees C."
Meanwhile, growers in Parana continued to enjoy optimal conditions.
"In the last four years we have had record production in this state and 1997 looks to be going the same way," said Fernando Muraru, agronomist at the Cotriguacu cooperative in Cascavel.

He predicted Parana would produce between 6.4 and 6.5 million tonnes this year, but added this could have been even higher had lack of financing not prevented many farmers from investing more in their crop.
"Soil moisture is ideal and it's raining every day," said Muraru. "The outlook is very positive."
